prompt: Turn pricing, procurement, and cross-sell theses into a finance-valid 100-day plan.
input: Fictional planning inputs. Industrial distributor baseline £40m annual EBITDA, not finance-reconciled. Theses: £3m annual pricing gross benefit with £0.4m recurring churn/mix disbenefit and 70% realization probability; £2m annual procurement benefit, zero recurring cost assumed, 80% probability and £0.3m one-off implementation cash paid regardless of success; £4m cross-sell revenue potential with unknown incremental margin, acquisition cost and probability. No monthly ramp or finance validation exists. CCO owns pricing, COO procurement, Sales Director cross-sell, CFO baseline/attribution. Build an explicit value bridge and 100-day plan. Separate annual run-rate, one-off cash and actual first-year results; exclude untested cross-sell from committed value.
rubric: Separates potential, underwritten, and realized value
Assigns one owner, milestones, dependencies, and red flags
Shows gross benefits, costs, and net value without double counting
critical_guardrails: Do not deduct one-off cash from recurring annual run-rate
Do not call unreviewed potential underwritten or realized, or gross cross-sell revenue EBITDA
output:
# Distributor value plan — current-session response

## Executive answer

£3.42m is a risk-weighted annual planning hypothesis, not underwritten or realized value. The £40m EBITDA baseline is not reconciled. Validate pricing/procurement first and keep the £4m gross cross-sell revenue potential out of the committed EBITDA plan.

## Financial bridge

Pricing annual value = (£3m − £0.4m conditional recurring churn/mix disbenefit) × 70% assumed realization probability = £1.82m.
Procurement annual value = £2m × 80% assumed probability − £0 assumed recurring cost = £1.60m.
Combined annual run-rate = £3.42m. These probabilities are fictional planning inputs, not empirically validated success rates.

The £0.3m procurement implementation cash cost is one-off and paid regardless of success. It is not deducted from recurring annual run-rate. £3.42m − £0.3m = £3.12m is only a full-year-equivalent net cash illustration before ramp. Actual first-year cash/EBITDA cannot be forecast without rollout timing, ongoing costs, accounting and attribution. Cross-sell revenue is not incremental EBITDA; margin, cost and capacity are missing. No initiative is finance-approved.

## 100-day plan

| Initiative / one accountable owner | Days 0–30 | Days 31–60 | Days 61–100 | Dependency and stop trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pricing / CCO | Reconcile segment price, mix and baseline with CFO; test elasticity | Pilot rules and exceptions in two segments | Scale only after net contribution/retention review | Needs clean transaction/mix data; pause on material volume or customer harm |
| Procurement / COO | Reconcile spend and supplier/service baseline with CFO | Negotiate two categories and verify service continuity | Contract and track attributable savings, not quote reductions alone | Needs contract and quality review; stop on continuity or quality breach |
| Cross-sell validation / Sales Director | Establish unique account overlap and margin economics | Test a limited conversion pilot within delivery capacity | Fund or stop based on incremental contribution and payback | Exclude overlapping pricing benefit; stop if positive contribution is not demonstrated |

CFO owns baseline, disbenefit, one-off and monthly ramp validation. Weekly owner reviews resolve dependencies; monthly finance reviews distinguish unreviewed, forecast, validated and realized benefit. Escalate missed critical milestones or material value erosion to the sponsor. Day 30 approves pilots only after reconciled baselines; day 100 approves scale only on measured evidence and an explicit finance sign-off.
